stages.title: What is a community?
stages.hook: Who lives on your street? Who do you see every day? What do all those people share?
explain: A community is a group of people who live or work near each other. A village is a community. A street is a community. A school is a community too.
People in a community share places, like a park or a market. They help each other. They make the place better together.
Every community has people who help decide things. In some places that person is called a mayor. Different countries use different names and different ways to choose.

example.q: Ana lives on a street with 6 houses. Her school has 3 classes. Which is a community?
steps: A community is people who share a place.
The street has people who share a place.
The school also has people who share a place.

analogies.home: A family shares a home. A community is like a bigger family that shares a place.
analogies.city: A city is a big community with many streets, shops and schools.
analogies.nature: Bees live in a hive and each bee has a job. A community is like that, with people who help each other.

stages.mnemonic: Community: we share a place, we share a space, we help each other.
terms: People who live or work near each other and share places.
A person who lives near you.
A leader of a town or city in many places.

misc.wrong: A community is only people who look the same.
misc.right: A community is people who share a place. They can be very different from each other.

stages.limits: Some people say community means people who share a hobby or a belief, even far apart. Here we talk about places.

trip.prompt: Look at the pictures. Can you find people sharing a place?

questions.q: What is a community?
o: People who share a place
One house with a single family
A kind of food people share
Animals that live in a zoo
questions.why: A community is people who live or work near each other and share a place.

questions.q: Which one is a community?
o: A school with pupils and teachers
A big box of old shoes by a river
A lonely cloud floating in the sky
A pencil lying in a school bag
questions.why: A school has many people who share a place.

questions.q: What do people in a community often share?
o: A park or a market
Every toy they own
Their dreams every night
The same name
questions.why: People share places like parks, markets and roads.

questions.q: Sam is new on your street. What is a kind thing to do?
o: Say hello
Hide from him
Ignore him
Take his toys
questions.why: Saying hello helps make a friendly community.

questions.q: Do all people in a community have to be the same?
o: No, they can be different
Yes, everyone must be alike
Only the grown-ups differ
Only the children do
questions.why: Communities have many kinds of people who share a place.

questions.q: A street has 4 houses on one side and 3 houses on the other side. How many houses are on the street?
questions.why: 4 + 3 = 7 houses.

questions.q: Match the place to its job.
questions.why: Each place helps the community in a different way.

questions.q: A mayor is a leader in...
o: Many towns and cities
Only in a zoo or on a farm
Only on a ship out at sea
Nowhere in the whole world
questions.why: In many places a mayor leads a town or a city. Other places use other names.

questions.q: Why do neighbours help each other?
o: It makes life better for everyone
It is a secret rule from long ago
It makes the rain fall down
Nobody really knows why
questions.why: When we help, the whole community is happier and safer.

questions.q: Which is the biggest?
o: A city
A house
A room
A table
questions.why: A city has many streets and houses in it.

panel.q: Two neighbours do not agree about a game. What helps a community most?
o: Listen to each other and find a fair way
Shout the loudest until you win the game
Never speak to each other ever again
Break the game so nobody can play it
panel.why: Listening and finding a fair way keeps a community friendly.

panel.q: Why is a school a community?
o: Many people share it and help each other
It has a roof, a door and a window
It is painted in bright, happy colours
It is much bigger than most houses
panel.why: Sharing a place and helping each other is what makes a community.

panel.q: A new family moves in. What makes the community stronger?
o: Welcoming them
Keeping them out
Laughing at them
Not telling them anything
panel.why: Welcoming people makes a community friendly and strong.

teach.model: A community is people who live near each other and share places like a park or a school. They help each other. For example, your street is a community.

points.ask: What do people do for each other?
Can you give me an example?

stages.title: Public buildings and services
stages.hook: Who pays for the school and the library? Can everybody use them?
explain: Public buildings belong to the whole community. A school, a library and a clinic are public buildings. People can use them.
A service is help that people get. Teaching is a service. Taking away rubbish is a service. Keeping a library open is a service.
The town pays for these with money from the community. The money comes from taxes. A tax is money people pay to share the cost of things we all use.

example.q: A town has 1 library and 2 schools. How many public buildings is that?

analogies.home: At home, everyone helps pay for food that all share. A town shares the cost of the library.
analogies.city: The library is like a big shared bookshelf for the whole city.
analogies.sport: A public pitch is a ball field that every team can use.

stages.mnemonic: Public means for you and for me.
terms: Help that people get, like teaching.
Money people pay so we can share the cost of things.

misc.wrong: A public building belongs to one person.
misc.right: A public building belongs to the whole community and is for everyone.

trip.prompt: Look at the pictures. What can people do in a library?

questions.q: Which is a public building?
o: A library
A private bedroom
A shop owned by one family
A pocket
questions.why: A library is for the whole community.

questions.q: What is a service?
o: Help that people get
A big hat for a party
A kind of birthday cake
A sign you see on a road
questions.why: A service is a helpful job done for people, like teaching.

questions.q: Who can use a public park?
o: Everyone
Only one person
Only the mayor
Nobody
questions.why: Public means for everyone.

questions.q: The town needs money for a new school. Where does some of it come from?
o: Taxes
Chocolate
Clouds
Sand
questions.why: Taxes are money people pay together to share costs.

questions.q: The clinic is closed. Who is hurt most?
o: People who need a doctor
Birds in the tall trees
Nobody, it does not matter
The moon, far away in the sky
questions.why: A clinic helps people stay well, so closing it hurts those who need it.

questions.q: A town has 3 schools. Each school has 10 classrooms. How many classrooms are there in all?
Put these in order from smallest to biggest.
questions.why: A room is in a house, houses are on a street, streets are in a city.

questions.q: Match the building to what it gives.
questions.why: Each public building gives a service.

questions.q: Why do we share the cost of a library?
o: One person could not pay for all of it
Books are very heavy to carry home
Libraries are cold, so they need sharing
A library is too small for one person
questions.why: By sharing the cost, everyone can use it.

questions.q: A village has no clinic. What could help?
o: Asking the leaders to plan one
Doing nothing and just waiting
Closing the school to save money
Hiding the problem from everyone
questions.why: Leaders and the community can plan new services together.

panel.q: The town can pay for only one new thing: a bigger library or a new clinic. How can leaders choose fairly?
o: Ask what most people need
Pick the one the mayor likes
Pick the one that is nearest to the mayor
Flip a coin without asking
panel.why: Asking people about their needs is a fair way to choose.

panel.q: Why should a public building have a ramp?
o: So people who use wheels can get in
It looks funny to most people
It is slippery when the weather is wet
To keep the birds out of the building
panel.why: Public means for everyone, so everyone must be able to enter.

panel.q: A library lets you borrow a book and bring it back. Why is that good?
o: Many people can read the same book
Books grow back again every week
Books are free to burn for warmth
Books do not matter to anyone at all
panel.why: Sharing means more people get to enjoy each book.

teach.model: A public building belongs to the whole community. Anyone can use it. A library and a school are examples. People pay taxes to share the cost.

points.ask: Who can use a public building?

stages.title: Rules and responsibilities
stages.hook: What would happen if everyone drove on any side of the road?
explain: A rule is something we all agree to do. Rules keep us safe and fair. A rule can say: wait for your turn.
A responsibility is a job you should do. Putting away your toys is a responsibility. Being kind is a responsibility.
Good rules are fair to everyone. People can talk about a rule if it is not fair. Different places have different rules, but many rules are to keep people safe.

example.q: There is a rule: walk, do not run, in the school hall. Why?

analogies.home: At home, a rule might be to wash hands before eating. It keeps everyone healthy.
analogies.sport: A game has rules so that every team plays fair.
analogies.city: Traffic lights are rules that help cars and people cross safely.

stages.mnemonic: Rules are the fences that keep us safe; responsibilities are our jobs.
terms: Something we all agree to follow.

misc.wrong: Rules are only to stop you having fun.
misc.right: Rules keep people safe and make things fair for everyone.

trip.prompt: Look at the pictures. How does a traffic light help people?

questions.q: Why do we have rules?
o: To keep people safe and fair
To make people feel sad and cross
To use up all of the paper
There is no reason for them at all
questions.why: Rules help people stay safe and treat each other fairly.

questions.q: Which is a responsibility?
o: Putting away your toys
Eating ice cream on a hot day
Taking a long nap after lunch
Watching the clouds go by
questions.why: A responsibility is a job you should do.

questions.q: A red traffic light means...
o: Stop
Go fast
Dance
Sing
questions.why: Red means stop so people can cross safely.

questions.q: Mia pushes in front of the line. Is that fair?
o: No, everyone should wait for their turn
Yes, because she is faster than us all
Yes, because we are only playing a game
Only if she smiles at everyone nicely
questions.why: A fair rule gives everyone a turn.

questions.q: A rule seems unfair. What is a good thing to do?
o: Talk about it politely with leaders
Break it in secret and tell no one
Shout at the person who is in charge
Run away and hide from the problem
questions.why: Good communities can talk about rules and change them fairly.

questions.q: Put these steps in order for crossing a road safely.
questions.why: Stop first, then look, wait, and cross.

questions.q: A class has 8 children. Each child has 2 jobs, like giving out books and cleaning the board. How many jobs are there in all?
Match the rule to why it helps.
pairs: Wear a helmet on a bike
questions.why: Rules often are fair, safe or kind.

questions.q: If there were no rules on a playground, what could happen?
o: Someone could get hurt or left out
Everything would be perfect and safe
It would rain candy all day
Nothing at all would change
questions.why: Rules protect people and make sure everyone can join.

questions.q: Who must follow rules in a community?
o: Everyone, including leaders
Only the children in the town
Only the visitors who come
Only people with dogs
questions.why: Fair rules are for everybody.

panel.q: A rule says no bikes on the footpath. Why might that be a good rule?
o: People walking could be hurt
Bikes are bad for towns
Footpaths do not like wheels
It makes bikes go faster
panel.why: Bikes can bump walkers, so the rule protects people.

panel.q: Leaders must follow the rules too. Why?
o: So the rules are fair for all
Leaders like to do homework
Leaders never break any rules
It is just a joke for fun
panel.why: Fair rules apply to everyone.

panel.q: A rule can change when people find it does not work. Is this good?
o: Yes, rules should help people
No, rules can never ever change
Only on Mondays at noon
Only when someone shouts loudly
panel.why: Rules should be checked and changed if they do not help.

teach.model: Rules help keep people safe and fair. A rule can be to wait your turn. A responsibility is a job we should do, like tidying up.

stages.title: Community helpers
stages.hook: Who helps when there is a fire? Who helps when you are ill?
explain: Community helpers are people who do jobs that help others. A firefighter puts out fires. A nurse cares for sick people. A teacher helps you learn.
Other helpers work in ways we do not always see. A bus driver takes people to work. A person who cleans streets keeps us healthy. A baker makes bread.
Every helper matters. We say thank you. In many places helpers are paid by the town or by a business. Different places have different names for these jobs.

example.q: The bell rings. A child falls and cuts a knee. Who helps?
steps: A nurse or a first-aid helper cares for people.

analogies.home: At home, someone cooks, someone cleans. In a town, helpers share the jobs.
analogies.sea: On a ship, the captain, the cook and the engineer all help the ship sail.
analogies.music: In a band, each player does a different part so the song sounds good.

stages.mnemonic: Helpers help: fire, health, school and street.
terms: A person whose job helps others.
A person who puts out fires and rescues people.
A person who cares for sick or hurt people.

misc.wrong: Only people in uniforms are helpers.
misc.right: Many people help, like bakers, bus drivers and cleaners.

trip.prompt: Look at the pictures. What tools does a firefighter use?

questions.q: Who puts out fires?
o: Firefighter
Baker
Teacher
Painter of houses
questions.why: Firefighters put out fires and rescue people.

questions.q: Who helps you learn to read?
o: Teacher
Farmer
Bus driver
Builder
questions.why: Teachers help children learn.

questions.q: Who keeps the streets clean?
o: Street cleaners
Pilots
Singers on stage
Painters of walls
questions.why: Street cleaners help keep the town healthy.

questions.q: You feel very ill. Who should you tell?
o: A trusted grown-up
A stranger on the street
Nobody at all
A teddy bear
questions.why: Tell a trusted grown-up who can get a doctor or nurse.

questions.q: What would happen if bus drivers stopped for one day?
o: Many people could not get to work or school
Nothing would change for anyone at all
There would be more ice cream for everybody
The rain would stop for the whole day
questions.why: Many people depend on buses, so every helper matters.

questions.q: Match the helper to the job.
questions.why: Each helper does a job that helps others.

questions.q: A fire station has 5 firefighters on each of 3 teams. How many firefighters is that?
A helper does a good job. What is a kind thing to say?
o: Thank you
Go away now
Say nothing at all
Hurry up, please
questions.why: Saying thank you shows respect.

questions.q: Is a baker a community helper?
o: Yes, they make food people need
No, bakers never help anyone
Only on Fridays each week
Only if they wear a tall white hat
questions.why: Many jobs help people, not just uniforms.

questions.q: Why do towns need many kinds of helpers?
o: People need many different things
To make lots of noise in the town
To fill up all of the empty buses
There is no reason for it at all
questions.why: People need food, health, learning, safety and more.

panel.q: A town has plenty of firefighters but only one nurse for 1,000 people. What could leaders do?
o: Plan to add more nurses
Send the firefighters all home
Close the only clinic
Do nothing about it at all
panel.why: Leaders should look at what people need and balance the helpers.

panel.q: Why do helpers need training?
o: To do the job safely and well
To waste some of their time
To grow taller each year
To feel sleepy while they work
panel.why: Training helps them keep people safe.

panel.q: Is it fair to treat all helpers with respect?
o: Yes, each job matters
No, only some
Only if they are famous
Only grown-ups matter
panel.why: All jobs that help others deserve respect.

teach.model: Community helpers do jobs that help other people. A firefighter puts out fires and a nurse cares for sick people. We should say thank you.

points.ask: How can we show we care?

stages.title: Keeping neighbourhoods clean
stages.hook: What happens to rubbish if nobody picks it up?
explain: Rubbish is things we throw away. If it stays on the street, it smells and can make people ill. Animals can get hurt too.
A bin is a place for rubbish. Some places also have bins for paper, plastic or food. Sorting helps us reuse things. Reuse means using something again.
Cleaning is a team job. Workers collect rubbish. We help by putting litter in bins. Towns pay for trucks and workers with money from the community.

example.q: There are 10 bits of litter. You pick up 4. How many are left?

analogies.home: At home we put plates in the sink and rubbish in the bin to keep the house tidy.
analogies.nature: A clean stream helps fish to live. Litter can harm them.
analogies.city: Rubbish trucks come on set days to keep the street clean.

stages.mnemonic: Bin it, sort it, reuse it, keep it clean.
terms: Rubbish dropped in the wrong place.
Make old things into new things.

misc.wrong: One piece of litter does not matter.
misc.right: Many small pieces add up, so every person helps.

trip.prompt: Look at the pictures. What things can be recycled?

questions.q: Where should litter go?
o: In a bin
On the road
In a river
Under a bed
questions.why: A bin keeps the place clean and safe.

questions.q: What does recycle mean?
o: Make old things into new things
Throw things away anywhere you like
Eat the paper up
Paint a wall bright blue
questions.why: Recycling turns used materials into new things.

questions.q: Why is litter bad for animals?
o: They can get hurt or sick
They like it a lot, like a snack
It is a toy for them to play with
It makes them sing songs
questions.why: Animals can eat or get stuck in litter.

questions.q: You see a drink can on the grass. What is the best thing to do?
o: Put it in a bin or recycling
Kick it far into the road
Leave it right there on the grass
Hide it under a big bush
questions.why: Putting it in the right bin keeps the place clean.

questions.q: Which is a way to reuse?
o: Use an empty jar to hold pencils
Throw the jar into a stream
Smash the jar on the hard ground
Bury the jar deep in the garden
questions.why: Reuse means using something again.

questions.q: Mina picks up 7 bottles. Ravi picks up 5 bottles. How many bottles do they pick up together?
Put these in order: what happens to rubbish.
items: You put it in a bin
It goes to a sorting place
questions.why: Rubbish is collected and sorted so some can be reused.

questions.q: Match the item to its bin.
questions.why: Sorting helps recycling. Bin colours differ by place.

questions.q: Who helps keep a neighbourhood clean?
o: Everyone
Only the mayor
Only children
Nobody
questions.why: Cleaning is a team job.

questions.q: Rubbish is not collected for many days. What may happen?
o: It smells and attracts pests
It turns into gold coins
It grows into flowers
It becomes very quiet and clean
questions.why: Waste can spread germs and attract pests.

panel.q: A street has no bins, and litter is everywhere. What is a good first step?
o: Ask the town to put in bins and help clean
Blame one child for all of the litter
Do nothing and just walk on past
Give up and go home because litter wins
panel.why: Bins plus community help can fix the problem.

panel.q: Why might a town pay workers to collect rubbish?
o: It is a big job that helps everyone
Because the trucks like to be busy
It is a fun game for the workers
To make more smells all around town
panel.why: A shared service is paid for by the community.

panel.q: Is it fair that everyone helps keep the place clean?
o: Yes, we all share it
No, only some should
Only visitors
Only adults
panel.why: Shared places need shared care.

teach.model: We put litter in bins so the street stays clean and safe. Workers collect it. Some of it can be recycled and used again.

stages.title: Public parks
stages.hook: Why do cities keep green places where nobody lives?
explain: A public park is a green place for everyone. People play, walk and rest there. Trees give shade and clean the air a little.
Parks need care. Gardeners cut grass and plant trees. People keep parks tidy. Towns pay for parks because they help everyone be healthy and happy.
A good park is for everyone. It has paths wide enough for wheelchairs and pushchairs. It has shade and safe places to play.

example.q: A park has 12 benches. 5 are broken. How many benches work?

analogies.home: A park is like a big shared garden for the whole street.
analogies.sport: Parks have fields where teams can play.
analogies.nature: Trees and flowers give homes to birds and bees.

stages.mnemonic: Park: play, air, rest, and keep it nice.
terms: A green public place for play and rest.
A cool place out of the sun.

misc.right: Parks are for people of every age.

trip.prompt: Look at the pictures. What do people do in parks?

questions.q: What is a public park?
o: A green place for everyone
A private garden for one family
A shop that sells cars
A kitchen at home
questions.why: A public park is open to everyone.

questions.q: Why do trees help in a park?
o: They give shade and homes for birds
They are very loud and noisy
They make a lot of rubbish for us
They block the whole sky and stop the sun
questions.why: Trees give shade and homes to animals.

questions.q: Who looks after a public park?
o: Gardeners and the community
Nobody looks after it at all
Only one little child does
Only the birds that live there do
questions.why: Towns pay gardeners, and people help by keeping it tidy.

questions.q: A park path has big steps. Who might not be able to use it?
o: A person in a wheelchair
A little bird in the tree
A butterfly flying in the air
A tree standing by the path
questions.why: Steps are hard for wheelchairs, so smooth paths help everyone.

questions.q: Which keeps a park nice?
o: Putting litter in the bin
Picking all of the flowers
Breaking the benches
Making holes in the grass
questions.why: Careful use keeps a park nice for everyone.

questions.q: A park has 6 swings and 4 slides. How many play things is that?
Put these in order from seed to shade.
questions.why: A seed grows slowly into a tree.

questions.q: Match the thing to what it gives.
questions.why: Each part of a park helps.

questions.q: Why does a town pay for parks?
o: They help people be healthy and happy
So the grass has a place to sleep
Because parks like to sing to people
There is no reason for them at all
questions.why: Parks give free places to play and rest.

questions.q: A hot day. Where will you feel cooler?
o: Under a tree
On a hot road
Next to a wall in the sun
On a roof
questions.why: Trees give shade and keep places cooler.

panel.q: A town can build a car park or keep a park. What should leaders ask?
o: What do people need most?
Which is shiniest?
Which is louder?
What did we do last year?
panel.why: Leaders should look at needs and ask the community.

panel.q: Why should a park be safe at night?
o: So people can use it with less danger, for example with lights
So it looks scary and quite empty to everyone
So that bats can come out and play there
So that nobody comes to the park at all
panel.why: Lights and clear paths help people feel and be safe.

panel.q: A park has no shade. Who is helped most by planting trees?
o: Everyone, especially small children and older people on hot days
Nobody, because shade does not matter on hot days
Only the gardener who works there every day
Only dogs, because they get very hot in the sun
panel.why: Shade protects people from too much sun.

teach.model: A public park is a green place for everyone to play and rest. Trees give shade. People keep it tidy so everyone can enjoy it.

points.ask: How do we look after it?

stages.title: Roads and transport
stages.hook: How do people and food get from one place to another?
explain: Roads, paths and rails help people and things move. A bus, a bike and a train are kinds of transport.
Roads need rules and care. Crossings help people walk safely. Workers fix holes. Signs tell us where to go.
A bus carries many people at once. That uses less space and less fuel for each person than lots of cars. Towns plan roads, paths and buses so everyone can get around.

example.q: A bus carries 30 people. A car carries 3 people. How many cars would be needed to carry 30 people?

analogies.home: Hallways in a house help you go from room to room. Roads do that for a town.
analogies.sea: Ships use sea lanes the way cars use roads.
analogies.nature: Ants follow paths to food. People follow roads.

terms: Ways of moving people or things.
A place made for walking across a road.
A vehicle that carries many people.

misc.right: Roads are shared by walkers, cyclists, buses and cars.

trip.prompt: Look at the pictures. How do people travel in different cities?

questions.q: Which carries the most people at once?
o: A bus
A bicycle
A scooter
A skateboard
questions.why: A bus can carry many people at once.

questions.q: What does a crossing help with?
o: Walking across a road safely
Parking a car for a long time
Cooking food in a kitchen
Painting a picture on a wall
questions.why: Crossings are made for people to cross safely.

questions.q: Why do we look both ways before crossing?
o: To check that no vehicle is coming
To see the birds up in the sky
To count the cars on the road just for fun
To tie your shoes up again
questions.why: Looking helps you stay safe.

questions.q: Who fixes holes in the road?
o: Road workers
Teachers
Bakers
Doctors at the clinic
questions.why: Roads need care from workers paid by the community.

questions.q: Why is a bus good for a city?
o: It moves many people with less space and fuel each
It is loud and makes noise all over the street
It is slow on purpose to annoy people
It has only one seat, and it is for the driver
questions.why: Sharing a vehicle uses less road space per person.

questions.q: A bus has 25 people on it. 8 get off and 5 get on. How many people are on the bus now?
Put the steps in order to ride a bus.
items: Get on and pay or show your pass
questions.why: First wait, then board, then sit safely.

questions.q: Match the sign colour to the meaning at a traffic light.
pairs: Slow down and get ready to stop
questions.why: Meanings can differ a little in places, but red means stop almost everywhere.

questions.q: A child uses a wheelchair. What helps most at a kerb?
o: A ramp
A big step
A wall
A hole
questions.why: Ramps let more people move around.

questions.q: If a town had no buses, who would struggle most?
o: People without a car
People who have a car
Nobody would struggle at all
Only the pilots
questions.why: Buses help people who cannot drive or afford a car.

panel.q: Many children walk to school by a busy road. What could leaders add?
o: A safe crossing
More noise
A shorter school day
A bigger car
panel.why: A crossing makes the walk safer.

panel.q: Why do towns build bike lanes?
o: So people can ride safely and keep roads less busy
To hide the bikes away from everyone
To make the roads much shorter
There is no reason for bike lanes at all
panel.why: Lanes separate bikes from cars and give people a choice.

panel.q: Leaders can pay to fix one road. How can they choose fairly?
o: Look at which road is most used and most unsafe
Pick the street where the leader lives
Pick one with no thought at all
Pick the shortest road in town, whatever it needs
panel.why: Use evidence about need and safety.

teach.model: Roads, paths and buses help people move. A bus carries many people. We use crossings and look both ways to stay safe.

stages.title: Helping others
stages.hook: Can one small kind act change a whole day?
explain: Helping others means doing something kind. You can share, listen, or carry a bag for someone. Small acts matter.
Some people need more help than others. A person who is ill, old, very young or new to a place may need help. Helping does not mean doing everything for them. It means asking what they need.
Communities help too. A food bank gives food to families who need it. A town can plan services so people are not left out. People can give time or money to help.

example.q: A food drive needs 20 tins. The class brings 12. How many more are needed?

analogies.home: At home, you help set the table. It makes the day easier for all.
analogies.sport: In a team, players help each other, not only themselves.
analogies.nature: Bees work together to feed the hive.

terms: Caring about others and acting on it.
A person who helps without being paid.
A place that gives food to people who need it.

misc.right: Anyone can help, with time, kindness or skills.

trip.prompt: Look at the pictures. What are volunteers doing?

questions.q: What is a volunteer?
o: A person who helps without being paid
A kind of sweet red fruit
A person who drives a big town bus
The leader of a whole town
questions.why: A volunteer gives time to help.

questions.q: A friend drops their books. What do you do?
o: Help pick them up
Walk away and say nothing
Laugh at them
Take one of the books
questions.why: Helping is a kind thing to do.

questions.q: An older neighbour has heavy shopping. What is a good way to help?
o: Ask, 'Can I carry that for you?'
Grab it without asking them at all
Ignore them and walk right past
Tell them to hurry up, please
questions.why: Asking shows respect.

questions.q: What does a food bank do?
o: Gives food to people who need it
Sells new cars to families
Teaches maths to big classes of children
Fixes the roads all around town
questions.why: Food banks share food with families in need.

questions.q: Why do communities help people in need?
o: Everyone may need help sometime
It is a trick to get something back
To get lots of toys in return
There is no reason at all
questions.why: We are all safer and happier when we help each other.

questions.q: Four friends each give 3 tins of food. How many tins is that in all?
Put these in order for helping well.
items: Help in the way they want
Say it was nice to help
questions.why: Asking first makes sure the help is useful.

questions.q: Match the helper to the help.
questions.why: There are many ways to help.

questions.q: Is it ok to help a person who looks different from you?
o: Yes, everyone deserves kindness
No, we should stay away
Only if they look just like you
Only if they ask twice first
questions.why: Kindness is for everyone.

questions.q: Why is it good to ask before you help?
o: The person knows what they need
It is a rule made for robots only
It wastes lots of time
It is rude to ask anyone
questions.why: Asking helps you give the right help and respects them.

panel.q: A new child at school speaks a different language. What is a good way to include them?
o: Invite them to play and use pictures or gestures
Leave them alone on their own all day
Laugh at the words they say
Move away and play with someone else instead
panel.why: Including people helps everyone belong.

panel.q: A town has little money. How can it still help people?
o: Ask for volunteers and plan carefully
Do nothing and wait for lots of money
Hide until the problem has gone away
Close down everything in the town
panel.why: Volunteers and good planning stretch a small budget.

panel.q: Why should we thank volunteers?
o: They give their time
They are bored at home
They are paid a lot of money
It is just a joke
panel.why: Thanks shows we notice their effort.

teach.model: Helping means doing something kind for someone. We ask what they need first. A volunteer helps without being paid. Small acts can make a big difference.

points.ask: How do we know what to do?

stages.title: Making fair decisions
stages.hook: Four children want the last slice of cake. How can you choose in a fair way?
explain: A decision is a choice. A fair decision treats people in a way that is the same and honest. Everyone gets a say or a turn.
One fair way is to vote. Everyone raises a hand or puts a mark. The choice with the most votes wins. Another way is to take turns. Another is to share equally.
Leaders also make decisions. Fair leaders listen first. They give reasons. They try not to favour friends. Different places choose leaders in different ways, but fairness matters everywhere.

example.q: 10 children vote: 6 want a picnic and 4 want a movie. What wins?

analogies.home: At home, dividing a pizza so each person gets the same size is fair.
analogies.sport: In a match, the referee uses the same rules for both teams.
analogies.music: In a band, each person gets a turn to lead the song.

terms: Treating people the same and honestly.
A way to choose, where each person counts.

misc.right: A fair way gives everyone a chance to be heard.

trip.prompt: Look at the pictures. How do people vote in different places?

questions.q: Which is a fair way to choose a game?
o: Everyone votes
The loudest child chooses
The oldest child always chooses
Nobody plays
questions.why: A vote gives everyone the same say.

questions.q: A vote has 5 for the red team and 3 for the blue team. Who wins?
o: Red team
Blue team
Both
Nobody
questions.why: 5 is more than 3.

questions.q: What is a fair leader like?
o: Listens and gives reasons
Ignores what people say
Favours his or her own friends
Never speaks to anyone
questions.why: Fair leaders listen and explain.

questions.q: There are 2 children and 1 apple. What is a fair way?
o: Cut it into two equal halves
One child gets the whole apple
Throw the apple away
Hide the apple from both
questions.why: Equal halves are fair.

questions.q: Someone loses the vote. What is a kind thing to do?
o: Accept it and still be friends
Shout at the others very loudly
Stop playing with everyone for good
Take the prize for yourself
questions.why: Good communities accept fair results and stay kind.

questions.q: In a class vote, 9 children want story time and 7 want drawing. How many more votes does story time have?
Put these in order for a fair vote.
questions.why: First hear the choices, then vote, count and act.

questions.q: Match the problem to a fair fix.
questions.why: Different problems need different fair methods.

questions.q: Why should leaders give reasons for decisions?
o: People can understand and check them
To make their speeches very long
To hide things away from the people
To sound loud and strong
questions.why: Reasons help people trust a decision.

questions.q: Is it fair if a leader always picks their friend's idea?
o: No, that favours one person
Yes, that is always fair to all
Only if the friend is very nice
Only on Mondays
questions.why: Fairness means not favouring friends over others.

panel.q: Eight children want the only ball. Which plan is fairest?
o: Make a list and take turns
Give it to the tallest
Give it to the one who shouts
Put it away forever
panel.why: Turns give everyone the same chance.

panel.q: A group votes, but one shy child did not get to speak. What could help next time?
o: Ask each person for their idea before voting
Skip the voting and just guess the answer
Pick only the ideas that are the loudest
Stop the group meeting for good
panel.why: Hearing quiet voices makes decisions fairer.

panel.q: Different countries choose leaders in different ways. What stays important?
o: The process is fair and honest
The leader is tall
The flag is red
Votes are secret from everyone forever
panel.why: Fairness and honesty matter in every system.

teach.model: A fair decision treats people the same. We can take turns, share equally or vote. A fair leader listens and explains why.
